vertical_slice: Dock Ward environs -> collapsed warehouse -> fissure -> Area 1 -> Area 2

source_basis.source_priority: Official/private adventure facts override procedural interpretation.

coordinate_frame.provenance: Platform adaptation anchored to the existing validated World Slice regions; these coordinates are not adventure-source facts.

source_grounded: Jolly's Lamp Emporium is an unassuming, ramshackle shop among other unassuming, ramshackle shops.
A collapsed warehouse stands next door.
Nearby shop/apartment occupants watch warily from shutters.
Three Waterdeep City Watch members stand near the warehouse.
A halfling Gray Hands spy watches the area while pretending to be a drunken passerby.
procedural_interpretation: Use a coherent lower-Dock-Ward street segment rather than an isolated facade.
Provide believable neighboring facades, alleys, rooflines and distant architecture beyond the playable footprint.
original_worldbuilding: Non-interactive dock-district clutter may include handcarts, awnings, drainage, mooring/warehouse hardware and restrained street debris when it does not contradict the source.

source_grounded: Surviving portions of the warehouse contain no crates, boxes, barrels, wares or other stored goods.
Near the missing door, walls, ceiling and floor have collapsed into a deep sinkhole fissure.
A hemp rope is anchored firmly in the rubble and descends into the darkness.
The fissure descends at an angle.
procedural_interpretation: Keep the warehouse visually sparse; rubble, broken framing and collapsed envelope carry the scene instead of cargo props.
The rupture must read as a jagged structural failure, not a square hole.

source_grounded: Earthquake damage exposed an older tunnel network beneath the warehouse.
Many side passages are blocked by rubble.
The traversable route leads from the fissure toward the lost shrine through the adventure areas.
procedural_interpretation: Use broken timber, rubble, exposed earth/stone and a clear descending path to visually connect warehouse construction to subterranean worked stone.

source_grounded: The fissure ends at a level floor of worked stone.
Dust, debris, rocks and pieces of warehouse wood are spread across the floor.
The south passage is blocked; the passage continues north.
Two pairs of human-sized boot prints head north.
Smaller fissures, holes and cracks riddle the passage.
Twenty feet around the descent point is difficult terrain.
Six giant rats arrive first; three more arrive about one round later.
procedural_interpretation: Represent the side cracks as visibly dangerous/non-traversable geometry without player-visible debug markers.
Boot prints are subtle environmental evidence, not glowing clue markers.
hidden_semantics: Rat spawn/arrival timing remains encounter metadata rather than visual telegraphing.

source_grounded: The chamber is rectangular and shows no earthquake damage.
Buttresses and columns support its walls and ceiling.
Four floor-set pools contain blue, green, clear and cloudy liquids.
Wall carvings depict robed figures submerging themselves in the pools.
A large ornate double door with an ornate carved lock stands at the far end.
Each pool is 10 feet deep with sheer sides.
map_grounded: The four pools occupy the four quadrants of the chamber around a central group of columns.
The double door is on the chamber's far/east wall.
procedural_interpretation: Use repeated masonry modules for the intact architecture and distinct pool materials for immediate visual readability.
The door trap and magical trial outcomes remain hidden mechanics; the room should not expose them through debug materials.

implementation_rules: Prefer installed 3D Canvas/Mapmaking Pack assets and materials before custom GLB.
Custom geometry is reserved for source-specific shapes that installed assets cannot represent convincingly, especially the warehouse fissure and bespoke Area 2 relief/lock details.
Every generated placeable must carry flags.acq.semantic_id, flags.acq.build_id, provenance and classification.
Apply changes idempotently with expected scene revision checks.
Player-visible geometry must not expose traps, secrets or GM-only semantics.
World context extends beyond the battle grid so the slice reads as a location in Waterdeep rather than a test stage.
